s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal and abnormal imaging findings in the temporal bone
salient_findings: Nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
key_facts: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness
Initially treated with oral steroids
No hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
Nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
MRI showed a 5 × 10-mm irregular lesion in the right mastoid
Lesion had heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast
Expansion of the fallopian canal and erosion of the posterior external auditory canal on CT
Specimen consisted of cartilage on gross examination
Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei on microscopic examination
Staining positive for S100 and negative for KI-67

shortlist.label: Chondroma

raw.rationale: The presence of a nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal, expansion of the fallopian canal, and erosion of the posterior external auditory canal, along with the microscopic findings of pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei and staining positive for S100, support the diagnosis of chondrosarcoma.

rejected.label: Chondroma
rejected.why: Chondroma is typically a benign tumor and the presence of pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei suggests a more malignant process.

rejected.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
rejected.why: The specimen consisted of cartilage on gross examination, which is not typical for schwannoma.

rejected.label: Glomus jugulare tumor
rejected.why: Glomus jugulare tumor typically presents with pulsatile tinnitus and hearing loss, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Myxoid chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: While myxoid chondrosarcoma is a subtype of chondrosarcoma, the provided information does not specifically suggest myxoid features, making chondrosarcoma a more general and appropriate diagnosis.
